partial.type_support: rosidl_typesupport_c/cpp dispatched to matching introspection C/C++; dynamic serialization/take loads an optional rosidl_dynamic_typesupport plugin at runtime; non-introspection typed publish/take and middleware type discovery remain unsupported
partial.qos: KEEP_LAST, lifespan, deadline metadata, reliability transport subset, ROS 2-compatible profile checking across reliability, durability, deadline, liveliness kind, and liveliness lease duration with ERROR/WARNING reason aggregation, and rmw_dds_common-backed BEST_AVAILABLE endpoint adaptation at create time. The 5/5 BEST_AVAILABLE artifact covers publisher/subscription discovery selection, zero-endpoint defaults, mixed-publisher liveliness/max-lease selection, actual-QoS reporting, and frozen policy after churn
partial.reliability: source-sequence ACK/NACK repair and unrecoverable-loss notices carry subscriber identity; only reliable readers emit ACK/NACK and participate in rmw_publisher_wait_for_all_acked snapshots, while best-effort readers detect sequence gaps without requesting repair. If a requested reliable sample has already left writer history, the writer emits a targeted loss notice and the reader advances without NACKing forever; repair admission/budget/attempt exhaustion uses the same terminal path. The three policy-terminal paths each pass 5/5 two-container Docker/netem runs with clean teardown. rmw_publisher_wait_for_all_acked waits for every still-matched reliable endpoint and honors finite and zero timeout behavior. In addition to the local two-reader 5/5 control, a four-container UDP/router/netem gate repeats 5/5: a deliberately delayed second remote ACK yields RMW_RET_TIMEOUT at 1/2 ACKs and OK at 2/2, with one DATA and both ACKs observed and forwarded by the router. Full DDS writer-history/resource-limit semantics and DDS wire interoperability are not claimed
partial.wait_sets: subscriptions, services, clients, domain-scoped automatically triggered graph guard conditions for local/remote add/remove/descriptor/QoS changes and remote lease expiry, max_conditions enforcement with zero meaning unbounded, null-entry rejection, active/same-context validation, and exact entity-owner node validation. Unread status readiness is implemented for every non-invalid Jazzy rmw_event_type_t: offered/requested deadline missed, liveliness lost/changed, offered/requested incompatible QoS, message lost, publisher/subscription incompatible type, and publication/subscription matched. A 5/5 Docker matrix executes seven production probes per round (35/35 components), checks initial/cleared not-ready controls, and consumes ready statuses through rmw_take_event. Separate event-family DDS semantics and remote production boundaries remain scoped
partial.transport: UDP reference transport/router plus POSIX SHM local path and de-duplicated SHM-local/UDP-remote hybrid; UDP large-frame fragmentation/reassembly is implemented for RMW endpoints with router fragment passthrough. The legacy ngtcp2/GnuTLS H3 gateway probes remain available as a subprocess fallback, including async enqueue/drain, session/tp/token file plumbing, repeated local/netem soak, publish POST, and take GET evidence. An optional in-process ngtcp2 0.12.1/GnuTLS 3.8.3/nghttp3 0.8.0 H3 client is integrated into both rmw_publish and on-demand rmw_take_serialized_message: the Docker/netem proof executes 128 publishes plus one take over one QUIC v1 connection, one verified TLS handshake, 129 bidirectional streams, 128 same-connection reuses, zero reconnects, three client-native qlogs plus three server qlogs, and an untrusted-CA fail-closed control. Its final independent rmw_publish and rmw_take calls run from two threads and rendezvous into concurrent POST/GET streams before either response is driven; an explicit paired transport API provides a second positive control. The pairing window is opt-in and unmatched calls fall back to normal single-stream execution. A stateful aioquic QUIC v1/H3 FleetQoX gateway now validates real FleetRMW data frames, keeps bounded per-domain/topic history, deduplicates publisher sequence numbers, and maintains independent consumer replay cursors; a 5/5 Docker/netem proof exercises exact replay through verified TLS, persistent client sessions, qlogs, and fail-closed HTTP status propagation. A separate 5/5 six-container netem gate loads a client certificate/key into the in-process GnuTLS client and requires mutual TLS at the gateway: one trusted client is admitted while missing-certificate and unrelated-CA clients are rejected before state mutation. An additional certificate signed by the trusted CA but carrying a mismatched SPIFFE-style publisher URI SAN receives HTTP/3 403 because opt-in identity binding requires the URI suffix to equal the FleetRMW publisher_id; it also cannot mutate gateway state. A current, correctly signed client CRL is validated at startup and a CA-trusted certificate whose serial is listed is rejected during TLS authentication. The aioquic 0.9 compatibility path uses a guarded private TLS hook, so native upstream client-auth support, broader fleet identity policy, online revocation/rotation, accepted 0-RTT/resumption, clustered durability, congestion/admission integration, and production readiness remain unclaimed
partial.actions: verified through rclpy action decomposition, upstream rclcpp Nav2 lifecycle management, CI-light real Nav2 planner/controller plugin configure lifecycle transport, planner/controller lifecycle activation with repeated dynamic /tf over FleetRMW, upstream Nav2 ComputePathToPose planner action execution with repeated /map plus /tf, upstream Nav2 FollowPath controller action execution with repeated /map plus /tf plus /odom, repeated same-pose NavigateToPose BT pipelines, a short moving-base NavigateToPose BT pipeline where a fake base consumes /cmd_vel and publishes dynamic /odom and /tf through FleetRMW, an extended single-goal moving-base pipeline at x=1.2, a direct upstream nav2_behaviors Spin recovery action through behavior_server, a NavigateToPose BT RecoveryNode branch that intentionally fails ComputePathToPose then executes Spin, a scoped NavigateToPose pipeline that executes Spin before successfully planning and following a short path, a repeated two-run recovered-success smoke wrapper, a repeated unobstructed 1m-plus moving-base workload for long-navigation smoke coverage, a planner-level static-obstacle repair/replan probe where a blocked occupancy grid aborts ComputePathToPose and a clear-map update succeeds, a full-stack NavigateToPose retry-after-clear probe where a blocked static map aborts the first goal and a clear-map retry succeeds with fake-base motion, a same-goal NavigateToPose BT retry probe where a blocked static map triggers planner failure, a real Wait recovery action runs, an external clear-map repair arrives during the same goal, and the goal succeeds with fake-base motion, and upstream Nav2/RMF concurrency-8/16/32/64/128/256/512/1024/2048 action/service workloads; no dedicated native rmw_action ABI and no dynamic obstacle/costmap-clearing policy claim
partial.events: new message/request/response callbacks are supported; QoS event object init/fini and callback setters are supported; offered/requested deadline missed events are produced by a timer after the first publish/receive or on the next publish/receive after a deadline gap; publication/subscription matched, reliability/durability/deadline/liveliness-incompatible QoS, and exact type-incompatible events are produced for local endpoints, with matched, reliability/durability/deadline-incompatible QoS, and exact type events also produced for UDP-learned remote graph endpoints; local liveliness incompatibility covers automatic/manual kind, slower offered lease, missing offered lease, both offered/requested events, and a compatible control across 5/5 Docker runs. Remote advertisement renewal is deduplicated and explicit remove or graph-lease expiry updates matched and finite-liveliness changed state; subscription message-lost events are produced for KEEP_LAST queue overwrite, best-effort source-sequence gaps after a configurable grace interval, and subscriber-targeted reliable writer-history, repair-budget, repair-attempt, or repair-admission exhaustion, with first-sample join baselining and late repair/reorder suppression. The reliable history-exhaustion path passes 20/20 two-container Docker/netem runs; a second artifact proves budget=0, max-attempt=1, and strict-admission rejection 5/5 each. Duplicate notices are merged into one sample/event and every process tears down cleanly. Local MANUAL_BY_TOPIC liveliness lost/changed events are produced for finite lease timeout and explicit reassert. AUTOMATIC finite-lease publishers are renewed by the middleware while alive; a 5/5 Docker control remains idle for six lease periods with no false lost callback or wait readiness. Remote MANUAL_BY_TOPIC publishers use an independent wire assertion sent by explicit assert and publish; a 5/5 two-container UDP/netem artifact proves idle expiry without unmatching, both reassert paths, publisher-side lost callback/wait/take, and independence from periodic graph renewal. A second 5/5 remote artifact proves independent state across two simultaneous publishers, alive/not-alive removal, exact aggregate liveliness counts, and remove/recreate churn of a third endpoint while expiry remains distinct from matching. A local 5/5 scale artifact proves exact aggregate transitions across 64 MANUAL_BY_TOPIC publishers, independent keepalive/expiry/reassert/removal halves, and 16 idle SYSTEM_DEFAULT publishers that remain alive for six finite lease periods. A two-container UDP/netem scale artifact repeats 5/5 with 64 remote MANUAL_BY_TOPIC publishers, exact half-expiry/reassert/all-expiry/removal and matched deltas, 96 expiries, 32 reassertions, and matching preserved through expiry. Default/non-expiring leases retain alive/remove lifecycle events without false timeout for SYSTEM_DEFAULT, AUTOMATIC, MANUAL_BY_TOPIC, and BEST_AVAILABLE in a 5/5 artifact; UNKNOWN and deprecated MANUAL_BY_NODE endpoint inputs fail closed. Unread statuses for all eleven non-invalid Jazzy event types become ready through rmw_wait and are consumed through rmw_take_event in a 5/5 aggregate matrix (35/35 components). Four repeated real UDP/netem source artifacts additionally cover callback/wait/take paths for all eleven event types over 35 executions. Full DDS message-lost/resource-limit semantics, deprecated participant-wide DDS liveliness semantics, complete DDS/vendor-specific remote event semantics, and the full QoS/type compatibility matrix are not implemented
partial.content_filters: subscription content-filter set/get stores and returns expression parameters, marks the subscription CFT-enabled, supports dynamic reconfigure and empty-expression disable, and enforces parameterized = != <> > >= < <= predicates plus SQL-like AND/OR/NOT precedence, parentheses, LIKE, BETWEEN, IN/NOT IN, IS NULL, and IS NOT NULL on key-value text and std_msgs/String-style payloads. Missing fields retain SQL unknown through negation; malformed expressions and missing parameter references fail closed. The full DDS SQL expression dialect and typed-field reflection are not implemented
partial.security: rmw_init_options security-options lifecycle, enclave copy, context init copy, shutdown, fini, opt-in FleetQoX publish allow/deny rules, and a scoped SROS2-generated DDS permissions, governance, and local identity validation path are covered by repeated Docker probes and the stress/security campaign. FleetRMW verifies permissions.p7s and governance.p7s at runtime, validates local identity before rmw_init, and enforces permissions plus Governance access-control across topic/service/Action paths. The UDP AEAD v2 envelope uses AES-256-GCM with HKDF-SHA256 PSK session derivation/reuse/rotation, signed random salts, nonce replay tracking, SROS2 X.509 peer signatures, identity allowlists, CA-chain validation, and CRL revocation; valid paths and tamper, unauthorized-identity, untrusted-CA, revoked-certificate, and missing-key controls pass 5/5. This is not DDS-Security interoperability or forward-secret asymmetric key exchange, and production PKI/transport hardening remains unimplemented
partial.benchmark_reporting: unified report aggregator normalizes existing JSON summary artifacts and capability claim boundaries without rerunning benchmarks, including the 8/16/32-robot three-seed split-scope and same-hop DDS/Cyclone/Zenoh comparisons, ns-3 artifacts, the OMNeT++ 6.4/INET 4.7 Docker runtime and matched routed-P2P bounded-parity matrix, and Docker stress/security campaign artifacts. The same-hop study permits delivery/reliability comparison only: FleetRMW forwards raw frames while the common baseline relay deserializes and republishes std_msgs/String, so latency and architectural superiority remain disallowed
partial.serialization_size: exact recursive size for statically bounded introspection C/C++ messages; artificial bounds for unbounded fields are unsupported
partial.allocations: publisher/subscription allocation init/fini allocate a type-support-bound, mutex-protected payload scratch buffer; typed and serialized publish/take reuse its capacity. A 5/5 Docker artifact performs eight publish/take pairs per process with exact use counts, stable 65536-byte capacity, zero payload-scratch growths, and rejection of an uninitialized allocation. Frame encoding, reliability history, transport queues, and application-message deserialization can still allocate, so deep/all-hot-path preallocation remains unclaimed
